issues.description: Return type annotation for dd_create_zero_state in the template does not match the solution (and the intended usage). The template declares dd_create_zero_state(num_qubits) -> DDNode and its docstring repeats this, while the reference solution implements and uses dd_create_zero_state returning a DD. This mismatch in annotated return type may confuse students (especially when reading type hints/docstrings) and could lead to incorrect assumptions about which object to construct/return.
issues.suggested_fix: Update the template annotation and docstring for dd_create_zero_state to match the intended/solution type: change the return type from DDNode to DD and update the docstring to state that the function returns a DD representing the n-qubit zero state. This keeps type hints, examples, and student expectations consistent with the solution and the rest of the codebase.

issues.description: The problem statement and the solution expect dd_create_zero_state to produce a DD representing the n-qubit |0...0> state, but the template's signature and docstring refer to/annotate the return type as DDNode. DD (the student-facing wrapper containing a node and weight) is the conceptual entity students are asked to construct and use throughout the exercise, whereas DDNode is an internal implementation detail. This mismatch (DD vs. DDNode) can confuse students about what to return and how to use other helper functions and tests (which operate on DDs). The template also does not import DDNode, making the annotation inaccurate and increasing the chance of implementation errors.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the template with the problem statement and solution by changing the dd_create_zero_state signature and docstring to indicate it returns a DD (not DDNode). Concretely, update the function annotation to -> DD and update the docstring to say it returns a DD representing the n-qubit zero state. Ensure the template uses the imported DD type (already imported) and removes/avoids referencing the internal DDNode in the public API.
